advances: Actual radial simplex bodies locally about a positive even sampled radius. The baseline normalized depth is Gamma_d.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Positive homothetic copies of $T_d$ are nested since $0\in\operatorname{int}T_d$. Minkowski combination at two real bases followed by radius concavity gives the actual convex body $C_r$, compact by continuity and with nonempty interior from positivity and the interior of $B$. Its complete sample is exactly the family $r_zT_d$ over $P$, with total mass $V_d\sum_z r_z^d$. For any fixed halfspace $J$,
$$
|\mu_r(J)-\mu_s(J)|\le V_d\sum_z |r_z^d-s_z^d|.
\tag{1}
$$
The right side is the measure of the sampled symmetric difference, by nestedness. This bound is uniform over all ambient halfspaces.

For compactness of the all-normal search, fix a finite base set, a source $(z_0,0)$ and arbitrary fibers strictly inside a centered ball of radius $H$. A nonvertical through-source cap has margin $u\cdot x+\alpha\cdot(z-z_0)$ with $\lVert u\rVert=1$. Restrict the base coefficient to $\operatorname{span}(P-z_0)$. Keep its row evaluations at $z-z_0$ fixed if they lie in $[-H,H]$, and otherwise impose the corresponding saturation constraint at $H$ or $-H$. This feasible closed polyhedron has a minimum-norm point. That point lies in the span of its active rows, since both small signs of a motion in their common kernel remain feasible. For an independent family with row matrix $D$ spanning the active rows and right sides $t$, the point equals $D^{\mathsf T}(DD^{\mathsf T})^{-1}t$. The empty family gives zero. There are finitely many row matrices and each entry of $t$ has absolute value at most $H$, so the norm is at most $K(P,z_0)H$. The new cap has the same actual fiber traces, with the same $u$, because the support bound is strict. This argument is independent of convexity of the bounded fibers. For the positive radial family, one $H$ works for all nearby samples. Nonvertical mass is continuous on the resulting compact parameter domain, since every limiting trace hyperplane is $d$-volume null.

At a centroid, a purely vertical closed through-source cap is strictly dominated by a nonvertical one. Multiply its base coefficient by a large finite factor and add any unit continuous normal. Every strictly sided fiber keeps its full or empty status, every tied fiber becomes a subset of its old full trace, and the own positive centroid fiber loses positive mass. A general containing cap can be tightened to pass through the source. For a nonvertical cap strictly containing a centroid, the tightening strictly reduces the mass in its own fiber, since that centroid is interior. Thus at every centroid an attaining nonvertical through-source cap exists and any minimizing cap has that form.

At $Y=(0,0)$ and the baseline $r^0$, apply the paired centroid-tail inequality 6a7d56e450b3126f to the equal-radius fibers at each pair $z,-z$, with thresholds $\pm\alpha\cdot z$, and to the own fiber at threshold zero. Their total is at least $Q_0$. The ordinary equality case in §1 of ea91e021ff1f4416 applies to the own positive simplex. Equality there requires the apex side of a cut parallel to a facet, precisely one of the directions $u_i$. The corresponding zero-tilt cylinders all take $Q_0$. In a canonical direction a pair with radius $r_z$ and shift size $s=|\alpha\cdot z|$ has total cap mass $[(d r_z+s)^d+(d r_z-s)^d]/d!$ for $0\le s\le r_z$. Strict convexity makes this larger than its zero-shift value when $s>0$. For $s\ge r_z$ one fiber is full, with mass $V_dr_z^d>2c_dr_z^d$, since $(1+1/d)^d>2$ for $d\ge2$. For $d=2$ the exact total in this latter range is $(9/2)r_z^2+(2r_z-s)^2/2$ up to $s=2r_z$, and $(9/2)r_z^2$ thereafter, from the remaining apex cap. Thus equality forces zero effective tilt and the baseline menu consists exactly of the displayed cylinders. On the compact domain there is a positive mass gap outside any small open neighborhoods of these normal parameters, provided the complement is nonempty. Estimate (1) preserves that gap uniformly relative to $Q_0$ under small sample changes.

At $Y$ in the chart of $u_1=e_1$, write the margin as $x_1+\sum_{j=2}^d\theta_jx_j+\alpha\cdot z$. At every fiber the retained apex remains $r_zv_1$, with strictly positive margin, and the other vertices have strictly negative margins for small chart parameters and nearby radii. The apex margin is $(d-\sum_j\theta_j)r_z+\alpha\cdot z$. The edge drops from the apex are $(d+1)r_z$ and $(d+1)r_z(1-\theta_j)$ for $j=2,\ldots,d$. Multiplying the edge fractions by the full simplex volumes and summing gives the exact mass
$$
\Phi(r,\alpha,\theta)=
\frac{\sum_z[(d-\sum_j\theta_j)r_z+\alpha\cdot z]^d}{d!\prod_{j=2}^d(1-\theta_j)}
=\frac{s^d}{\prod_{j=2}^d(1-\theta_j)}F_r(\alpha/s),
\qquad s=1-\frac1d\sum_{j=2}^d\theta_j.
\tag{2}
$$
The prefactor is at least one by AM–GM applied to $1,1-\theta_2,\ldots,1-\theta_d$, with equality only at $\theta=0$. All brackets are positive on a fixed small convex neighborhood in the effective $\beta$ variable. The $\beta$-Hessian there is $(d(d-1)/d!)\sum_z(d r_z+\beta\cdot z)^{d-2}zz^{\mathsf T}$, positive definite on $L$. At $r^0$ the gradient at zero vanishes by evenness. The implicit function theorem and strict convexity give the unique small critical point, smooth in the sampled array, and its exact minimum in this neighborhood. If $L=\{0\}$, the normal variable is absent and the same minimum statement is immediate. Shrink the normal charts so each $\alpha/s$ lies in the common convex neighborhood, then shrink the radius neighborhood so the optimizer is inside each chart. The permutation symmetries of $T_d$ give (2) in every canonical chart and leave $\alpha$ unchanged. Together with the compact gap this proves the true all-normal minimum and its complete bounded representative menu. For an original unbounded coefficient attaining the same minimum, its representative has the same continuous unit normal and exactly the same traces. Every representative trace is proper in a positive full-dimensional simplex, so its threshold is uniquely determined by the trace for the fixed direction. Therefore the original effective coefficient agrees at every base and hence on $L$. This recovers the complete original menu.

For $d=2$, the chart mass completes the square as
$$
\Phi=\frac{(2-\theta)^2 E}{2(1-\theta)}
+\frac{[\alpha+(2-\theta)G^\dagger b]^{\mathsf T}G[\alpha+(2-\theta)G^\dagger b]}{2(1-\theta)} .
$$
Here $E>0$ since it is the squared residual after orthogonal projection of the radius array onto functions $z\mapsto a\cdot z$, and its coordinate at $0$ equals $r_0>0$. Using $(2-\theta)^2/(1-\theta)=4+\theta^2/(1-\theta)$ gives the stated solution. At the baseline the Hessian in these chart coordinates is $\operatorname{diag}(G|_L,R(r^0))$. In general the angular Hessian at $\theta=0$ of the prefactor in (2) is $I_{d-1}-\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/d$, so the full baseline normal Hessian in $(\theta,\beta)$ is positive definite, with angular block $Q_0$ times that matrix and mixed block zero.

To compare source points, each permutation of the simplex vertices induces a linear volume-preserving action (in absolute determinant) on each sampled fiber. Its full point orbit averages to zero by barycentric symmetry. Depth is invariant under these actions, and its superlevel sets in ambient space are convex: a closed halfspace containing a convex combination contains at least one point in the combination. Hence a fiber centroid is a depth maximum on its fiber. At a nonzero base $z_0$, the baseline cap $x_1+\alpha\cdot(z-z_0)\ge0$ stays proper on all fibers for sufficiently small $\alpha$. Its actual mass is $\sum_z[d r_z^0+\alpha\cdot(z-z_0)]^d/d!$, whose gradient at zero is $-c_d z_0\sum_z(r_z^0)^{d-1}$. The tilt $\alpha=t z_0$ for small positive $t$ strictly decreases it below $Q_0$. Finiteness of $P$ and (1) preserve the strict competitor gap against $\tau(r)$ nearby. In the plane $d=2$, put $J=\max_z|z_0\cdot(z-z_0)|>0$, $H_2=\sum_z[z_0\cdot(z-z_0)]^2>0$, and $S_1=\sum_z r_z^0$. The choice $t=\min\{\min_z r_z^0/(2J),S_1\lVert z_0\rVert^2/H_2\}$ stays proper and decreases the cap mass by at least $(3/2)tS_1\lVert z_0\rVert^2$ by the same quadratic formula. At base zero, for any nonzero $x\in r_0T_d$, some $u_i\cdot x>0$ since the $u_i$ span and sum to zero. Shift the corresponding optimized cap through $(0,x)$. The cap shrinks everywhere and loses a positive own-fiber slab, since that fiber contains a ball about zero. Its mass is strictly below $\tau(r)$. This proves the unique global maximum and the stated normalized baseline.
statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge2$, and let $B\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a compact convex body whose complete integer sample $P=B\cap\mathbb Z^n$ contains $0$ and is centrally symmetric. Let $r^0:B\to(0,\infty)$ be continuous and concave with $r^0(z)=r^0(-z)$ at the sampled bases. Put $L=\operatorname{span}P$, $v_0=(-1,\ldots,-1)$, $v_i=v_0+(d+1)e_i$ for $1\le i\le d$, $T_d=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_d\}$, $V_d=(d+1)^d/d!$, and $c_d=d^d/d!$. For positive continuous concave $r$ on $B$ write $r_z=r(z)$ and take $C_r=\{(z,x):z\in B,\ x\in r(z)T_d\}$ with actual mixed set $S_r=C_r\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. Use summed fiber $d$-volume $\mu_r$, and let $h_r(y)$ be its infimum over closed ambient halfspaces containing $y$. There is a neighborhood of the sampled array $(r^0_z)$ such that, for every compatible $r$ with sample in that neighborhood, the unique deepest actual point is $(0,0)$ and its raw depth is
$$
\tau(r)=F_r(\beta(r)),\qquad
F_r(\beta)=\frac1{d!}\sum_{z\in P}(d r_z+\beta\cdot z)^d .
$$
Here $\beta(r)\in L$ is the unique small solution of $\sum_z z(d r_z+\beta\cdot z)^{d-1}=0$, and every bracket at the solution is positive. The full minimizing cap menu at $(0,0)$, modulo positive scaling and integer-coordinate coefficients invisible on $P$, is $u_i\cdot x+\beta(r)\cdot z\ge0$ for $u_i=e_i$ $(1\le i\le d)$ and $u_0=-\sum_i e_i$. Every fiber has maximum depth at its centroid and each nonzero-base centroid has strictly smaller raw depth than $\tau(r)$. At the baseline, $\tau(r^0)=Q_0=c_d\sum_z(r^0_z)^d$, with normalized depth $\Gamma_d=c_d/V_d$.

For $d=2$, write $G=\sum_z zz^{\mathsf T}$, $b=\sum_z r_z z$, $R=\sum_z r_z^2$ and $E=R-b^{\mathsf T}G^\dagger b$, where $G^\dagger$ inverts $G$ on $L$ and vanishes on $L^\perp$. Then $\beta(r)=-2G^\dagger b$ and $\tau(r)=2E$. All formulas include $P=\{0\}$, with no effective base-tilt variable.
title: Exact local all-normal depth for radial simplex fibers
